set_text.text: What is a warehouse space requirement?

A warehouse space requirement is the floor area your stock needs at its busiest, with room for people and pallet jacks to move. You get it from cases, pallets and stack height, then add aisles, dock and staging. It is the figure a lease should be sized on.
The floor your stock needs, not what a building holds. Start from 3,000 cases at peak and it works forward to 725 sq ft.
Offices, restrooms, a returns cage and forklift charging. The aisle share covers aisles, dock and staging only, so add the rest on top.
The calculator folds staging into the 45%. For a distributor, it tracks how many trucks you load at once, not how much stock you hold.
Who uses a warehouse space calculator
It is for independent food distributors working out how much building their stock needs. Anyone briefing a broker, signing a lease or adding a range should run it first.
